title: Prototype
description: The PRD made tangible enough that a PM can find what is wrong with it: one self-contained HTML file a person clicks through, plus this record of what it shows. Every shipped surface inside the MVP line has a screen; every functional requirement inside the line is on a screen or listed as uncovered — a non-functional requirement or a constraint is not a screen's to show. The builder writes the file and this record's screens, uncovered, notes and open questions; the runner owns identity, traces, the hashes, and each question's id and status, and keeps a blocker on the record until the PM answers it.

traces.description: What this prototype was built from. A PRD whose hash no longer matches makes the prototype stale — the badge, not a block.

file.description: Root-relative path of the one HTML file.

file_hash.description: sha256 of the file's bytes — the record is about this file and no other.

screens.description: Every screen the prototype shows. Ids are sticky — the same screen keeps its SCREEN-n across regenerations.

name.description: The name a person using the product would give this screen — not a component name.

surface_ref.description: The shipped surface this screen belongs to.

req_refs.description: The requirements this screen lets a person exercise.

uncovered.description: Requirements inside the line the prototype does not show. Skipping is allowed; skipping quietly is not.

notes.description: For the PM: what was ambiguous and which reading was taken, where the prototype cheats, what to look at first.

open_questions.description: What building it exposed that the PRD does not answer — as questions for the PM, never as decisions taken.

id.description: Minted by the runner and never issued twice. The same question keeps its PQ-n from build to build; one a ruling settled keeps the ruling's.

blocking.description: True if stories cannot be written until the PM answers this. A blocker stays one until answered: a rebuild that asks it as non-blocking, or no longer asks it, does not settle it.

status.description: Open until the PM answers it through the answer door, or approves a reaction that settles it.

questions_issued.description: The highest PQ number issued so far; a new question takes the next, so no id ever names a second question.

x-drift-checked.description: The pointers the content hash covers: the screens, what is uncovered, and the file itself.
